headlines.summary_en: Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for EMEA, Nohshad Shah, said Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's pledge to control inflation without specifying how he intends to achieve it has introduced new uncertainty for investors. headlines.title: 美银：若美联储说不清如何抗通胀方案美国国债就会重拾跌势
headlines.summary: 美国银行全球研究部的美国利率策略主管Mark Cabana认为，如果美联储不能更好地告诉大众它将如何实现2%的通胀目标，美国国债的跌势就会重新出现。 上周三将收益率推至近20年高位的长债抛售是一次“教科书式的通胀公信力冲击”。当天，美联储主席凯文·沃什在记者会上未能向投资者解释央行将如何抑制价格上涨。 “你有坚定的决心实现2%的通胀是很好，但除非你告诉我们你要怎么做到，否则我们是不会相信你的，” Cabana接受彭博电视采访时说，“而且你也骗不了债券，它会看穿你。”

headlines.title_en: BofA: If Fed Fails to Explain Inflation Strategy, U.S. Treasuries Will Resume Decline
headlines.summary_en: Mark Cabana, head of US rates strategy at BofA Global Research, believes that if the Fed fails to better communicate to the public how it will achieve its 2% inflation target, the selloff in US Treasuries will resume. Last Wednesday's long-end bond selloff, which pushed yields to nearly 20-year highs, was a 'textbook inflation-credibility shock.' That day, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh failed to explain to investors at his press conference how the central bank would curb price increases. 'It's great that you have firm resolve to achieve 2% inflation, but unless you tell us how you're going to do it, we're not going to believe you,' Cabana said in a Bloomberg TV interview. 'And you can't fool the bond market—it will see right through you.'

headlines.title_en: U.S. Treasury Raises July-September Borrowing Estimate to $739 Billion
headlines.summary_en: The US Treasury projects net marketable debt financing of $739 billion in the July-September quarter of 2026, assuming a cash balance of $950 billion at end-September. The estimate is $68 billion higher than the May projection, primarily due to anticipated lower net cash inflows. The Treasury expects to borrow $628 billion in the October-December quarter of 2026, assuming an $850 billion cash balance at end-December. In the April-June quarter of 2026, the Treasury financed $190 billion, roughly in line with the $189 billion estimate published in May. Further details on the Treasury's quarterly refunding will be released at 8:30 a.m. ET on August 5 (8:30 p.m. Beijing time).

headlines.title_en: U.S. Medium- and Long-Term Treasury Yields Fall More Than 4 Basis Points
headlines.summary_en: At the New York close on Monday (August 3), the US 10-year Treasury yield fell 4.90 basis points to 4.6857%, trading in a narrow range around 4.68%, hitting a session low of 4.6674% at 20:02 Beijing time. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 3.72 basis points to 4.2518%; the 30-year Treasury yield fell 4.19 basis points to 5.2295%, maintaining a low, narrow range. The 2s10s yield spread fell 0.373 basis point to +43.185 basis points. The 10-year TIPS yield fell 2.05 basis points to 2.4265%; the 2-year TIPS yield rose 1.02 basis points to 2.0968%; the 30-year TIPS yield fell 3.19 basis points to 3.0031%.

headlines.title: 广发证券：牛市中 什么时候才会出现“单顶”
headlines.summary: Citadel Securities（城堡证券）欧洲、中东和非洲区固定收益销售主管Nohshad Shah称，美联储主席凯文·沃什承诺控制通胀，却未说明具体打算如何实现，这给投资者带来了新的不确定性。 尽管沃什反复表示，央行需要遏制已连续五年超出目标的消费者价格涨幅，但美联储上周仍再次维持利率不变，即便有三名政策制定者支持立即加息。

headlines.title: 道明：干预势头可能短暂推动美元/日元跌至153
headlines.summary: 道明证券认为，干预的推动力可能会使美元/日元跌至153，但除非日本央行采取更多行动或美国财政部做出全面承诺，否则就只会暂时如此。“动能可能短暂推动美元/日元跌至153，但要没有日本央行的行动或美国财政部的全面承诺，我们不认为该货币对会大幅低于该水平，” Howard Du、Gennadiy Goldberg和Molly Brooks等策略师写道。“美日双边贸易动态、‘卖出美国’情绪复苏的风险、美国信誉恶化的风险、政治考量以及包括系统性冲击在内的风险，是我们相信美国财政部不愿全力托底日元的五大原因”。

headlines.title_en: TD: Intervention Momentum May Briefly Push USD/JPY to 153
headlines.summary_en: TD Securities believes intervention momentum could push USD/JPY to 153, but unless the Bank of Japan takes further action or the US Treasury makes a full commitment, it would only be temporary. 'Momentum could briefly push USD/JPY to 153, but without BOJ action or a full US Treasury commitment, we don't see the pair moving significantly below that level,' strategists including Howard Du, Gennadiy Goldberg, and Molly Brooks wrote. 'US-Japan bilateral trade dynamics, the risk of renewed 'sell America' sentiment, risks of deteriorating US credibility, political considerations, and risks including systemic shocks are the five reasons we believe the US Treasury is reluctant to fully back the yen.']
